arml-local-2016-team-01.prompt: All the shelves in a library are the same length. When filled, two shelves side-by-side can hold exactly $12$ algebra books and $10$ geometry books. All algebra books have the same width, as do all the geometry books, but algebra and geometry books have different widths. Three shelves side-by-side can hold exactly $15$ algebra books and $21$ geometry books. Compute the maximum number of geometry books that can fit on one shelf.

arml-local-2016-team-02.prompt: In the equation $\underline{A}\,\underline{B}\,\underline{C}+\underline{D}\,\underline{E}\,\underline{F}=\underline{G}\,\underline{H}\,\underline{I}$, each letter denotes a distinct non-zero digit. Compute the greatest possible value of $\underline{G}\,\underline{H}\,\underline{I}$.

arml-local-2016-team-03.prompt: If $\dfrac{\log_b a}{\log_c a}=2016$, then $\dfrac bc=c^k$. Compute $k$.

arml-local-2016-team-05.prompt: Compute the smallest positive integer $k$ such that $n^2-k$ is not a prime number for any positive integer $n\ge\sqrt k$.

arml-local-2016-team-06.prompt:
A *magic square* is an $n\times n$ grid of numbers where the numbers in each row and column add up to the same sum. Some of the values in the $5\times5$ magic square below have been erased. Compute $x$.

$$\begin{array}{|c|c|c|c|c|}\hline &1&&8&\\\hline 21&&12&&23\\\hline &25&&17&\\\hline 7&&22&&2\\\hline &20&&x&\\\hline\end{array}$$

arml-local-2016-team-07.prompt: Triangle $ABC$ is inscribed in circle $\omega$. It is given that $BA=BC=8$ and $AC=8\sqrt2$. The tangent to $\omega$ at $B$ intersects the tangents to $\omega$ at $A$ and $C$ at points $X$ and $Y$, respectively. Compute the area of quadrilateral $AXYC$.

arml-local-2016-team-08.prompt: In triangle $LMN$, it is given that $m\angle LMN=90^\circ$, $LM=5$, and $MN=12$. Point $P$ lies on the hypotenuse $LN$ such that $m\angle PMN=30^\circ$. If $PN=\frac{a-b\sqrt3}{c}$, where $a$, $b$, and $c$ are positive integers with no common factor greater than one, compute $a+b+c$.

arml-local-2016-team-09.prompt: Compute the sum of all positive integer values of $x$ such that there exists a positive integer $y$ such that $\frac1x+\frac1y=\frac1{10}$.

arml-local-2016-team-10.prompt: Compute the number of zeroes that $2016!$ ends with when written in base $2016$.

arml-local-2016-team-11.prompt: Compute the number of $2\times2$ matrices $M$ with the following properties: the entries of $M$ are integers between $0$ and $29$ inclusive; the determinant of $M$ is divisible by $30$.

arml-local-2016-team-12.prompt: Let $S$ denote the set of all $4^4$ functions from the set $\{1,2,3,4\}$ to itself. Three functions $f,g,h\in S$ are chosen randomly with replacement, with all functions having an equal probability of being chosen. Compute the probability that the following property holds: for every $y\in\{1,2,3,4\}$, there exists an $x\in\{1,2,3,4\}$ such that $f(g(h(x)))=y$.

arml-local-2016-team-13.prompt: Let $ABCDEF$ be a convex cyclic hexagon. Diagonals $AC$ and $BD$ meet at $X$ while diagonals $AE$ and $DF$ meet at $Y$. Suppose $AF=AB=3$, $BC=4$, $DC=DE=5$, and $EF=6$. Compute the ratio of the areas of triangles $CXF$ and $CYF$.

arml-local-2016-team-14.prompt: Initially, three vertices of an equilateral triangle are marked on a blackboard. Every minute, Alice marks the circumcenter of the triangle whose vertices are the three points on the blackboard, then randomly erases one of the four points on the board (each with probability $\frac14$). After one hour has elapsed, the probability that the three points on the blackboard form an equilateral triangle is $x$. Compute the nearest integer to $100x$.

arml-local-2016-team-15.prompt:
In the grid below, each of the letters $A$ through $P$ is equal to either $2$, $3$, $4$, or $5$. Exactly four letters are equal to each of the four numbers. Some of the sums of numbers in the columns are given, as are some of the products of numbers in the rows. Compute the $4$-digit number $\underline{A}\,\underline{F}\,\underline{K}\,\underline{P}$.

$$\begin{array}{cccc|c} A&B&C&D&\text{product }225\\ E&F&G&H&\text{product }128\\ I&J&K&L&\text{product }120\\ M&N&O&P&\\\hline \text{sum }10&\text{sum }12&\text{sum }15&&\end{array}$$

(The first three columns have the given sums; the products belong to the first three rows.)
